feature: Usage, models, speed, and reasoning controls
audit_feature: Choose analysis effort and inspect consumption
codex_behavior: Supported clients expose model and reasoning choices, usage information, and eligible speed modes. Faster modes can consume more allowance; access varies by model, plan, client and workspace. Delegated agents also consume resources.
trigger: The auditor starts a task, changes effort during work, or checks remaining capacity.
audit_action: Preserve the model/effort controls so an auditor can choose a quick document explanation or a deeper cross-file investigation and inspect what each run consumed.
outputs: Work product associated with its run
auditor_control: The auditor chooses among permitted options, changes direction, or stops work; the administrator retains applicable limits.
example: Use a modest effort setting to explain a workpaper formula, then a deeper setting to investigate inconsistent revenue evidence across several files.
adaptation_boundary: The mechanism transfers directly. A premium model or higher effort is not a professional assurance rating, and a model subscription is not assumed to fund a fork.

audit_enhancements.change: Show effort choices through task examples and preserve settings with relied-on outputs.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors need to understand what changed between two analysis runs without interpreting model settings as evidence quality.

subfeatures.audit: Choose an approved model for the audit task.
Adjust investigation depth and turnaround.
Inspect consumption across main and delegated work.

audit_feature: Run the audit assistant with an approved AWS model provider
codex_behavior: The local Codex experience can use Amazon Bedrock with AWS authentication. Hosted Codex Cloud and several OpenAI-managed integrations are unavailable on that path; capabilities vary by endpoint and region.
trigger: An organisation configures an approved provider, or an auditor selects an available provider profile.
audit_action: Retain the same audit workspace and local tool loop while sending permitted model requests through the configured Bedrock route.
auditor_control: Administrators approve provider configuration; auditors work within its available models and source permissions.
example: A team analyses locally held policy documents using its approved AWS model endpoint while keeping the same workpaper-review workflow.
adaptation_boundary: Changing inference provider does not make every connector or product feature available. Source access and tool traffic remain separate; hosted GitHub review is not inherited through this path.

audit_enhancements.change: Display provider and processing route with each engagement's effective policy.
audit_enhancements.why: A reviewer must distinguish where evidence was processed from where files were stored.

subfeatures.audit: Use the organisation-approved AWS principal.
Apply the permitted inference route for the assignment.
Explain unavailable audit actions before running them.

evidence.label: Bedrock client support and feature availability

audit_feature: Route audit model requests through the organisation's gateway
codex_behavior: Codex supports configured model gateways with provider identifiers, model aliases and credential resolution. Gateways must support expected streaming and tool behavior. This routing covers model requests; external tools may use different paths.
trigger: An administrator applies a model-gateway profile to the workbench.
audit_action: Keep the auditor's task experience while selecting models and sending permitted inference requests through the organisation's managed gateway.
outputs: Model responses through the configured route
auditor_control: Administrators determine permitted routing and credentials; the auditor can inspect the effective route and use available choices.
example: A firm exposes an approved 'document-review' model alias to auditors across different assignments.
adaptation_boundary: The gateway does not automatically mediate spreadsheet reads, browser activity, MCP tools or record-system writes. A complete data-path policy requires those routes to be considered separately.

audit_enhancements.change: Show model processing and evidence-source access as separate routes.
audit_enhancements.why: An auditor should not infer that all engagement data handling is governed by the model gateway.

subfeatures.audit: Offer organisation-approved analysis profiles.
Keep provider credentials out of engagement prompts.
Validate that routed models can complete supported audit tasks.

audit_feature: Use a local model for supported audit assistance
codex_behavior: The CLI supports local Ollama or LM Studio models through --oss and provider configuration. Non-interactive execution requires a configured local provider. This inference route does not establish offline support for all tools or integrations.
trigger: The auditor starts an eligible task using an approved local model.
inputs: Local work files and permitted tools
audit_action: Perform supported explanations, extraction or analysis planning with locally served inference while retaining the task and tool workflow.
auditor_control: The auditor or administrator chooses the local model and permitted tools; access to outside services stays separately controlled.
example: Explain a sensitive local control narrative with an approved local model before deciding which further analysis is appropriate.
adaptation_boundary: Do not promise equal capability, accuracy or speed to hosted models, or treat local inference as proof that every task is offline.

audit_enhancements.change: Expose a task capability check for the selected local model.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors should know when document understanding or tool use needs validation before relying on the result.

subfeatures.audit: Choose local inference for a supported audit task.
Retain the approved local model profile.
Fail clearly when an unattended local analysis lacks its model service.

audit_feature: Attribute unattended assurance runs to an authorised owner
codex_behavior: Eligible workspace access tokens support trusted non-interactive CLI/app-server runs as their creator. Service-account flows are distinct. Token creation permission and local Codex access are separate; expiration and revocation govern continued use.
trigger: A permitted automation starts an audit test without an interactive sign-in.
audit_action: Execute the configured test under an identifiable workflow owner and preserve that identity alongside the resulting work.
outputs: Usage associated with the execution identity
auditor_control: An authorised owner provisions, rotates and revokes credentials; the auditor defines the permitted task.
example: A monthly duplicate-payment check runs on a trusted machine using a dedicated workflow identity rather than an undocumented shared personal login.
adaptation_boundary: The fork's supported authentication route must be established independently. A model credential does not confer access to the payment source or authorise modifying it.

audit_enhancements.change: Present workflow owner, source-system identity and initiating event together.
audit_enhancements.why: Unattended findings must remain attributable when the person reading them differs from the executing principal.

subfeatures.audit: Start an authorised recurring test.
End or rotate an assurance job's access.
Use an organisational run owner where supported.

audit_feature: Inspect, accept and retain changes to audit work
codex_behavior: Supported Codex clients expose file and branch diffs, annotations, selective staging/reversion, commits, pushes and pull requests. Review can examine selected changes without editing the working tree.
trigger: An agent or auditor changes a work product, or requests review of an alternative revision.
audit_action: Show what changed in workpapers, calculations, narratives and supporting scripts; let the auditor inspect changes, comment, retain selected revisions, or restore an earlier version.
auditor_control: The auditor accepts or rejects changes and decides when to share the revised output. These choices remain separate from professional sign-off.
example: After revising a sampling workbook, inspect changed parameters and formulas, retain the corrected calculation, and reject an unrelated narrative edit.
adaptation_boundary: Preserve the review/acceptance experience. Semantic comparisons and safe merging for Office files require investigation; they cannot be assumed from text Git diffs, and auditors need not see Git terminology.

audit_enhancements.change: Compare audit-relevant cells, formulas, passages and evidence links.
audit_enhancements.why: Binary-file differences alone do not explain a changed conclusion.

audit_enhancements.change: Warn when a revision affects previously reviewed work.
audit_enhancements.why: A review of an earlier version may no longer cover the current one.

subfeatures.audit: Inspect and comment on meaningful workpaper changes.
Select or undo proposed revisions where the artifact supports it.
Retain revisions, compare alternatives and request review.

audit_feature: Run recurring assurance and preparation tasks
codex_behavior: Desktop schedules run recurring work in local project folders or isolated worktrees under configured permissions. Local files require an available computer/app. Web event-triggered tasks are a separate path; CLI lacks the Scheduled management interface.
trigger: An explicitly configured time or recurring interval arrives.
inputs: Applicable skills, tools and execution policy
audit_action: Repeat a defined audit analysis, evidence check or preparation routine and return its results to the designated task or separate run.
auditor_control: The auditor configures, edits, pauses or removes the schedule and reviews consequential conclusions or actions.
example: Every Monday compare the current vendor-master extract with the prior snapshot and report newly changed bank details for investigation.
adaptation_boundary: A schedule is not a business-event detector or a guarantee that work ran. Device availability, missing data and failures must remain visible; successful execution does not close a finding.

audit_enhancements.change: State the period, source version and last successful coverage for each run.
audit_enhancements.why: A quiet monitor should not conceal a missed week or stale extract.

subfeatures.audit: Repeat defined assurance procedures.
Run against current work or an isolated analysis copy.
Inspect results, pause monitoring and resume investigation.

evidence.label: Scheduled tasks and local execution limits

audit_feature: Speak instructions and steer audit work hands-free
codex_behavior: Supported desktop/mobile clients accept voice input and task interaction; existing task context can continue. Screen-context availability varies by platform. CLI voice is experimental, and this catalog does not establish general CLI audio-file ingestion.
trigger: The auditor starts voice input or continues a task through a supported voice surface.
audit_action: Let the auditor describe a discrepancy, ask for an explanation, change the analysis direction or review progress while working in their files.
auditor_control: The auditor can correct recognition errors, choose the active task and stop voice interaction.
example: While reviewing a reconciliation, say 'Explain why these three balances differ, then show the supporting transactions.'
adaptation_boundary: Task dictation does not automatically constitute a recorded interview, an accurate transcript, or evidence of another person's statement. Live screen support must be verified per client.

audit_enhancements.change: Confirm ambiguous amounts, dates and entity names before consequential use.
audit_enhancements.why: Misheard audit identifiers can direct testing toward the wrong population.

subfeatures.audit: Speak audit instructions and notes.
Redirect analysis while reviewing work.
Discuss the visible work item where the client permits it.

audit_feature: See which audit work is running or needs attention
codex_behavior: Desktop/mobile clients expose activity and unread or waiting work, with notifications when attention is needed. Available states, filters and alert behavior vary across clients.
trigger: A task finishes, encounters a problem, requires input, or has a new result.
audit_action: Keep the auditor aware of analysis progress and direct them to the exact task, finding or decision needing attention.
outputs: Link to the relevant run and result
auditor_control: The auditor decides what to open, prioritise or mute and can inspect the underlying task before acting.
example: While the auditor reviews a report in Word, a notice indicates that the access-review analysis found an unexplained privileged account.
adaptation_boundary: A 'done' indicator describes execution state, not a favourable assurance conclusion or reviewer approval.

audit_enhancements.change: Separate completed analysis, detected exception, missing evidence and review-needed states.
audit_enhancements.why: Each requires a different auditor response even if the agent turn has ended.

subfeatures.audit: Track concurrent tests and requested decisions.
Find analyses not yet inspected.
Bring consequential exceptions or blocked work to attention.

audit_feature: Optional floating companion for audit-task awareness
codex_behavior: The desktop app offers an optional animated companion that can show task activity and provide chat or voice entry above other windows. Appearance changes do not change agent behavior; custom companions are supported in specified surfaces.
trigger: The auditor enables the companion or interacts with it while another application is active.
audit_action: Preserve an optional lightweight entry and status surface while the auditor works in Excel, Word or another application.
auditor_control: The auditor can enable, personalise or hide the companion and chooses when to open the underlying task.
example: An auditor working in PowerPoint uses the floating companion to ask for the source behind a reported finding without navigating away first.
adaptation_boundary: This remains a peripheral experience feature. Animation neither establishes completion nor grants access to the foreground document.

audit_enhancements.change: Use discreet task labels and configurable notification detail.
audit_enhancements.why: Ambient cues should not expose client names or findings during meetings or screen sharing.

subfeatures.audit: Show audit-task activity beside existing tools.
Resume assistance from the companion.
Retain optional personalisation without changing analysis behavior.

audit_feature: Bring existing assistance setup into the audit workbench
codex_behavior: Supported Codex import flows transfer selected configuration and recent work from other agent tools. Coverage varies by client and source; imported tools may need reauthorisation. CLI import has local-session and recent-chat limits.
trigger: An auditor chooses to import supported setup or recent task context.
inputs: Eligible project folders and recent chats
audit_action: Bring reusable work conventions and selected task context into the audit workbench, showing what transferred and what needs attention.
auditor_control: The auditor chooses the import scope and inspects executable extensions and connections before relying on them.
example: An auditor moves existing analysis skills and engagement instructions from another agent tool into the new workbench.
adaptation_boundary: Importing agent setup is distinct from importing an entire audit system, preserving formal sign-offs or migrating authoritative records. Those require separate evidence and planning.

audit_enhancements.change: Identify engagement/client scope and source for imported memories and instructions.
audit_enhancements.why: Convenient migration must not silently mix confidential client context.

subfeatures.audit: Reuse established analysis procedures and preferences.
Continue supported investigative context.
Reconnect only the permitted evidence sources.

audit_feature: Share a fixed view of an audit investigation
codex_behavior: The documented macOS desktop flow shares a fixed read-only Codex thread snapshot. Audience controls differ by account. Supported visible content and diffs may appear, while original tool calls/results are omitted; links can be revoked.
trigger: The auditor chooses to share a completed or in-progress investigation snapshot.
audit_action: Prepare a fixed reviewable account of the investigation for an allowed recipient while preserving the distinction between a conversation snapshot and underlying evidence.
auditor_control: The auditor inspects the shared view, selects recipients where supported, and revokes the link when appropriate.
example: Share the discussion explaining a reconciliation exception with a manager before a review meeting.
adaptation_boundary: Recipients do not automatically receive workspace access, executable context or a complete evidence file. Sensitive details can survive automated redaction; a snapshot is not formal sign-off.

audit_enhancements.change: Show which supporting evidence and execution details are absent from the shared view.
audit_enhancements.why: The reviewer must know when to request the actual workpaper or evidence package.

subfeatures.audit: Share a fixed investigation narrative.
Limit review access under the supported account model.
Check disclosure and withdraw access to the snapshot.

audit_feature: Bound what an audit task can read, change and contact
codex_behavior: Codex separates filesystem and network restrictions, with OS-specific sandbox enforcement and distinct local/cloud resources. Named permission profiles are documented as beta; technical access differs from approval policy and source-system identity.
trigger: A task starts under a permission profile or requests an operation outside its current boundary.
audit_action: Run audit tools within the permitted work area, such as reading source extracts while writing analyses only to the engagement's output folder.
auditor_control: The auditor and administrator select permitted profiles within policy and review any eligible boundary-crossing request.
example: An agent tests a payroll extract and produces a results workbook while lacking authority to change the payroll source.
adaptation_boundary: A sandbox limits technical reach; it does not prove an auditor is entitled to a dataset or that analysis methods are suitable.

audit_enhancements.change: Explain access in terms of source evidence, working copies, outputs and external destinations.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors need to understand consequences without reading raw filesystem policy syntax.

subfeatures.audit: Separate source reading from permitted work-product changes.
Control permitted evidence and service destinations.
Make local, remote and cloud task reach visible.

audit_feature: Review consequential tool actions separately from audit conclusions
codex_behavior: Codex can route eligible interactive approval requests to a separate reviewer agent while retaining the same sandbox and policy. Routine permitted actions proceed normally. Computer Use prompts remain human-facing; automatic review is not a permission expansion. Documented configurations also include full-access/no-prompt operation, subject to applicable policy.
trigger: A task runs under its selected approval policy, and an action may require a decision or proceed under a configured no-prompt mode.
audit_action: Show the effective action authority and destination. Obtain decisions required by the configured policy; represent full-access/no-prompt operation explicitly when permitted, without treating that mode as professional approval.
auditor_control: The auditor retains appropriate action-approval authority; managed controls remain effective and professional approval stays distinct.
example: An analysis finishes locally; publishing its findings to a remote audit record requires a separately evaluated action permission.
adaptation_boundary: Tool permission, agent review of work, and professional sign-off are different decisions. An automated permission reviewer cannot certify evidence sufficiency or grant wider access. Including the broad mode in this inventory is not a recommendation to enable it; its scope must remain visible.

audit_enhancements.change: Use separate labels for permission to act, analytical review and professional approval.
audit_enhancements.why: The same word 'approve' must not conceal materially different authority.

subfeatures.audit: Review a proposed external or consequential action.
Evaluate eligible permission requests under the same policy.
Continue authorised analysis without bypassing a rejected action.
Represent a broad execution mode when policy permits it, with its effective reach visible

feature: Approved cyber model access (Daybreak / Trusted Access)
audit_feature: Use approved specialist cyber capabilities for authorised IT audit work
codex_behavior: Specialist defensive and advanced cyber model offerings have separate eligibility and provisioning requirements tied to identity, project and product surface. Such access is distinct from security scanning and does not itself establish retention privileges.
trigger: An authorised IT/IS audit task selects an available specialist cyber capability.
audit_action: Retain access to specialist reasoning for scoped security investigations while showing the specific model and task boundaries.
auditor_control: The authorised practitioner defines scope and consequential actions; organisation and service access restrictions continue to apply.
example: An IT auditor analyses supplied access-control code and configuration within an authorised assessment.
adaptation_boundary: No model entitlement authorises activity against arbitrary systems. The offering is not a ready-made audit methodology, and availability in Codex does not establish availability to a fork.

audit_enhancements.change: Bind the selected specialist capability to the authorised audit target and test scope.
audit_enhancements.why: A broad cyber model's capability should not be confused with the auditor's authority.

subfeatures.audit: Expose only approved specialist analysis choices.
Keep authorised engagement and service boundaries visible.
Distinguish reasoning access from executable security tests.

evidence.label: Models and Trusted Access for Cyber

audit_feature: Apply configured inspection to submitted audit prompts
codex_behavior: Eligible workspace-authenticated Codex flows can send submitted prompt text to Prisma AIRS for configured checks. Policies may alert or block. The documented scope excludes responses, tool results, files and images, and API-key sessions.
trigger: An auditor submits prompt text on an enabled, supported surface.
audit_action: Evaluate the prompt under configured disclosure and malicious-content checks before the supported workflow proceeds.
auditor_control: Administrators configure enforcement and failure behavior; auditors can revise blocked content or use an authorised path.
example: An auditor accidentally pastes sensitive identifiers into a prompt and receives a policy block before the supported submission proceeds.
adaptation_boundary: This narrow prompt inspection is not comprehensive evidence-file scanning or complete protection from prompt injection. Provider and client eligibility must be verified for a fork.

audit_enhancements.change: Explain which submitted audit material was inspected and which was outside coverage.
audit_enhancements.why: An auditor should not infer that an attached workbook was checked because the surrounding prompt was allowed.

subfeatures.audit: Check submitted audit instructions under policy.
Explain whether work can proceed.
Make inspection-outage behavior explicit.

audit_feature: Allow, review or forbid particular analysis commands
codex_behavior: Experimental command-prefix rules can allow, prompt or forbid commands running outside the sandbox; the most restrictive matching rule wins. These rules do not govern every app, browser, MCP or cloud action.
trigger: The agent attempts a command covered by a configured rule.
audit_action: Apply command-specific restrictions to repeatable analysis operations while preserving an understandable reason for allowed, prompted or blocked execution.
auditor_control: Administrators or authorised users set rules within policy; auditors respond to permitted prompts.
example: Permit an approved reconciliation script while requiring review before an export command sends results outside the workspace.
adaptation_boundary: Rules are one execution control, not a universal audit authorisation engine. Shell parsing and tool-path differences matter; allowing a command does not validate its findings.

audit_enhancements.change: Describe rules using the analysis action and destination as well as the command.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors need to understand a command's effect without judging executable names alone.

subfeatures.audit: Permit a matching command outside the sandbox where the effective policy allows it, with that authority explicit.
Review a consequential command invocation.
Block restricted operations and explain the controlling rule.

audit_feature: Apply organisational workbench policy consistently
codex_behavior: Enterprise controls distinguish orchestration policy from execution settings and support documented local/cloud overrides and inheritance. Managed requirements constrain personal configuration. ChatGPT Work Cloud has separate controls rather than inheriting Codex Cloud policy automatically.
trigger: A task starts, changes environment, or uses a managed capability.
audit_action: Calculate and display effective policy for the auditor's task, including execution, tools, extensions and approval behavior.
auditor_control: Administrators govern required policy; auditors retain choices only within the allowed range.
example: A firm permits local analysis for a client assignment but restricts cloud execution and unapproved extensions.
adaptation_boundary: Managed agent policy is not an audit methodology or assurance standard. Different execution surfaces require explicit coverage; one environment's settings cannot be presumed to govern another.

audit_enhancements.change: Explain the effective policy against the current assignment and chosen execution location.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors must understand why an action available elsewhere is unavailable for this work.

subfeatures.audit: Apply common assistance and approval rules.
Adapt permitted execution by location.
Show which organisation rule governs a disputed setting.

feature: Workspace roles, access, and user lifecycle
audit_feature: Manage access as audit-team membership changes
codex_behavior: Workspace roles, seats, local/cloud access and source permissions are distinct. Provisioning can use groups. Token suspension and revocation differ: restoring local access can reactivate suspended tokens unless they were revoked.
trigger: An auditor joins, changes assignment or role, or leaves the organisation.
audit_action: Provision the permitted workbench capabilities and track which access must be changed or ended when responsibilities change.
auditor_control: Administrators manage entitlements; engagement responsibilities determine appropriate access through the chosen policy.
example: A contractor finishes an engagement: remove the permitted workspace access and separately revoke or transfer the automation credentials they owned.
adaptation_boundary: Removing a seat does not necessarily revoke every external credential. Workspace roles alone do not implement preparer, supervisor or partner sign-off semantics.

audit_enhancements.change: Show engagement/client access and owned unattended jobs during reassignment or departure.
audit_enhancements.why: Confidentiality and continuity extend beyond the person's visible workspace seat.

subfeatures.audit: Grant the intended workbench access.
Distinguish local, cloud and tool access.
Suspend, revoke or reassign automation access deliberately.

audit_feature: Show whose access is used for each evidence source
codex_behavior: Connected tools use their configured authentication and permission scope. Remote-host tasks use host-side credentials and resources. The person steering a task can differ from the principal performing its source-system actions.
trigger: The task reads evidence or proposes an action through a connected source or remote host.
audit_action: Use the permitted source identity and make its relationship to the initiating auditor clear.
auditor_control: The auditor chooses an authorised connection where available; source-system permissions constrain what the task can do.
example: An access review reads a directory export using the approved read-only service account while the audit manager steers the investigation.
adaptation_boundary: Visible workspace membership and model identity do not determine source permissions. Shared files remain a separate access path with their own filesystem permissions.

audit_enhancements.change: Attach source account, entity scope and extraction context to relied-on results.
audit_enhancements.why: A complete-looking dataset may reflect a principal that could see only one subsidiary.

subfeatures.audit: Use the approved evidence-source account.
Respect read/write and entity boundaries.
Explain which host's credentials executed the analysis.

audit_feature: Keep evidence content separate from instructions to the agent
codex_behavior: Files, web pages, tool results and extension content may contain untrusted instructions. Hooks and plugin code can execute locally after applicable trust review; external tools may also cause side effects.
trigger: The agent encounters supplied evidence or a user enables executable extension behavior.
audit_action: Treat material under examination as evidence, follow the authorised task instructions, and expose extension trust and side-effect decisions.
outputs: Analysis that identifies its source material
auditor_control: The auditor controls task authority and permitted extensions; evidence providers cannot silently redefine the agent's mandate.
example: A supplied policy document contains text directing the assistant to omit a control weakness; the agent evaluates the document without treating that text as an instruction.
adaptation_boundary: Trust review does not guarantee an extension is harmless. Preserve the existing instruction/evidence boundary rather than assuming every connected source is trustworthy.

audit_enhancements.change: Make evidence-originated instructions recognisable in the investigation record.
audit_enhancements.why: Audit evidence can contain adversarial or misleading content that should itself be evaluated.

subfeatures.audit: Separate examined evidence from authorised instructions.
Inspect executable audit extensions before use.
Explain what an evidence tool may change.

feature: Enterprise usage analytics and compliance records
audit_feature: Inspect workbench adoption, operation and supported compliance events
codex_behavior: Enterprise usage analytics, the Analytics API, supported Compliance API events and local telemetry expose different information. They have separate permissions and coverage; none establishes a complete record of every action, input and model decision.
trigger: An authorised administrator or reviewer requests usage statistics or supported activity records.
audit_action: Report workbench adoption and operational activity while identifying which data source supports each statement.
auditor_control: Authorised roles select the scope and recipients; use of these records follows the applicable organisational purpose.
example: A team lead examines how often automated tests ran and separately checks available access events when investigating an account issue.
adaptation_boundary: Monitoring the audit tool is different from testing the client's controls. Usage counts do not measure assurance quality, and compliance events do not replace workpaper evidence.

audit_enhancements.change: Separate task volume, completed tests, exceptions and accepted work from token usage.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditor productivity and coverage cannot be inferred from consumption alone.

subfeatures.audit: Understand adoption and consumption.
Inspect supported administrative/activity records.
Provide authorised records with explicit coverage.

audit_feature: Retain and inspect task history with explicit coverage
codex_behavior: Codex persistence and histories vary by surface. Optional OpenTelemetry exports selected operational events and is off by default; prompt content is redacted by default. Telemetry, aggregate analytics and compliance records have different retention and coverage.
trigger: A user resumes an investigation, diagnoses a failed run, exports supported records or applies a retention policy.
audit_action: Preserve useful task continuity and diagnostics, and show what the retained record includes or omits.
auditor_control: The auditor or administrator chooses permitted retention and diagnostic settings; relying reviewers inspect the relevant evidence package separately.
example: Investigate why a reconciliation job stopped by examining retained tool status and rerun context, then keep the approved output in its designated record system.
adaptation_boundary: A chat transcript or telemetry stream is not automatically complete, immutable or compliant with the applicable audit-record policy.

audit_enhancements.change: Link retained task history to source versions, analysis artifacts and the designated record destination.
audit_enhancements.why: A later reviewer needs to distinguish recoverable working context from the relied-on audit record.

subfeatures.audit: Resume the investigation with retained context.
Diagnose task and tool failures.
Apply the chosen working-data policy transparently.

audit_feature: Describe an audit outcome and carry the work through to review
codex_behavior: This is a composition lens from ChatGPT Work, not a separate Codex feature: outcome-oriented requests combine research, tools, progress, steering and reviewable outputs. Its constituent mechanisms are mapped individually elsewhere.
trigger: The auditor describes the outcome, context and constraints of a task.
audit_action: Coordinate the existing task mechanisms to investigate, analyse, prepare an output, explain limitations and respond to review.
auditor_control: The auditor steers the task, challenges assumptions and decides how the output is used.
example: Ask for a reconciliation and an explanation of unresolved items, then inspect the workbook in the workbench or Excel.
adaptation_boundary: Retain this lens for composition coverage without counting it as an additional Codex capability. It does not require a prescribed engagement lifecycle for every task.

audit_enhancements.change: Express outcomes and completion criteria using the practitioner's work products.
audit_enhancements.why: The same task loop should serve standalone advisory work as well as formal audit procedures.

subfeatures.audit: Define the audit question and expected work product.
Investigate and revise with the auditor.
Inspect the output in the preferred tool.

audit_feature: Retain Codex's general agent foundation for audit work
codex_behavior: This is the catalog's composition lens for Codex's harness, execution, context, agents, extensions and controls. It summarises separately listed capabilities rather than introducing a further runtime feature.
trigger: An audit task invokes the general agent workflow.
audit_action: Preserve the general-purpose agent foundation while supplying audit-oriented tools, examples and work surfaces, with the original breadth still visible.
auditor_control: The auditor retains task steering, output review and configured permission decisions.
example: A single investigation searches documents, executes a reconciliation script, asks a specialist agent to inspect an exception and revises the report.
adaptation_boundary: A composition lens is not another feature count or proof that every hosted/client component is reusable. Required services and source boundaries remain research evidence.

audit_enhancements.change: Translate runtime outcomes into understandable audit activity while retaining technical detail on demand.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors need to follow the work without losing access to the actual analysis method.

subfeatures.audit: Coordinate evidence reading, analysis and output creation.
Sustain and delegate investigative work.
Keep tasks inspectible and bounded.

audit_feature: Use the Codex-derived experience across audit practices
codex_behavior: This entry is the user's audit-product composition lens, not an existing Codex feature. It asks how general agent capabilities adapt across practice areas, methodologies and the two proposed record modes.
trigger: An auditor applies their working method to a task or engagement.
inputs: Chosen external or built-in record mode
audit_action: Compose the mapped mechanisms around the auditor's actual work while retaining shared-file editing, task steering and review.
outputs: Work delivered to the designated record destination
auditor_control: The practitioner chooses methods and retains professional judgement; organisations define applicable roles and policies.
example: Use the same workspace experience for an operational advisory memo, a financial test and an IT access review, changing the task instructions and procedures.
adaptation_boundary: Record this as a product requirement lens without attributing audit functionality to Codex. A full built-in audit record lifecycle requires separate domain planning; the accepted two-mode ambition remains.

audit_enhancements.change: Provide adaptable terminology, procedures and artifact views without imposing one audit methodology.
audit_enhancements.why: Internal, external, advisory and IT/IS work need different domain content while sharing the same assistance experience.

subfeatures.audit: Apply the foundation to different audit practices.
Use the practitioner's procedures and terminology.
Support shared files and the designated record mode.

evidence.label: Underlying Codex customisation reference; audit composition is user-specified
